sources.note: Nothing on stress. 'Afenmai language' (sourced to Elimelech 1976) states two phonemic tones H/L with five surface tones, and that /ts dz/ are fricativized to /s z/ in the Aviele and South Uneme dialects; 'Edoid languages' cites Lewis, Ademola Anthony 2013 'North Edoid relations and roots' (PhD, Ibadan), which groups Uneme-Yekhee together.

sources.citation: Elimelech, Baruch. 1976. A Tonal Grammar of Etsako. UCLA Working Papers in Phonetics 35 (August 1976), 170 pp. [UCLA PhD dissertation; South Uneme = one of eight 'dialects of Etsako' in Appendix A comparative wordlist, pp. 120-164]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number L.SOC.120.Cf.5.9.8 (87); Widener Library, call number Philol346.20 vol.87); ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan (also lendable online at archive.org)
sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number L.SOC.120.Cf.5.9.8 (87); Widener Library, call number Philol346.20 vol.87
sources.note: Silent. Grammar of the Ekpheli dialect of Etsako (Yekhee); acknowledgements (p. viii) name Mr. Joseph Dirisu Onotu as consultant for South Uneme; p. 2 lists South Uneme (SU) among the eight dialects surveyed. Ch. III 'The Tonal System' (pp. 41-54 scanned): Ekpheli has five surface tones (high, low, falling, rising, downstep) and two systematic-phonemic tones (H, L), with downdrift/downstep. No occurrence of 'stress', 'accent' or 'prominence' in the scanned phonetic-correlates and tone chapters. The Uneme material is a 542-item tone-marked wordlist only; no Uneme-specific prosodic statement.
